method: Every v3 held-out case is paired by semantic judgement with its nearest v3 development case and the template difference is stated in words. Lexical measures (normalised-prompt equality, unit-and-number skeleton equality, and skeleton token Jaccard similarity) are supporting evidence only and never decide the review. Skeleton equality was checked across v1, v2 development, v2 held-out, v3 development and v3 held-out, and within each v3 set, with zero collisions.
coverageNotesForOperator: Missing activity reaching rule 11 is covered by WI-V3-H065 (a complete treadmill session that never names walking or running, oracle missingRequiredField ["activity"]). Generic whole-field parent coverage for missingRequiredField rests on the corrected H011 shape (H067), the sibling case (H066), the missing-plus-ambiguous case (H069) and development D005.
WI-V3-H012 treats 'jog on the treadmill' as indoorRunning under rule 5; ratified as the synonym coverage for v3.

WI-V3-H043 (stride length) is the only case that maps an unsupported target to bare steps. Within excessiveComplexity, WI-V3-H063 (unbounded alternation with no count) and WI-V3-H064 (recursive sequence) are pathed to steps as structural sequence problems, while the explicit finite counts in H060, H061 and the nested counted blocks in H062 use steps.repetitions.

WI-V3-H030 (belt lubrication) sits at the outOfDomain versus unsupportedOperation boundary and is ratified as outOfDomain []: treadmill maintenance is not a request about a workout, so the rule 7 addition (workout-related input asking for another operation) does not engage.
Scorer aliases use WI-V1-201 to 220 (development) and WI-V1-301 to 379 (held-out); the v2 verifier's WI-V1-1xx pattern must be widened by the harness-code slice.

heldoutNearestDevelopment.templateDifference: Development is a prose request ('warm up for 2 minutes at 3 km/h and 0%, then ...'); this case is three labelled lines with comma-separated values and no connecting verbs, so the model must read a tabular structure rather than a narrative one. Same plain-walk behaviour, every number different.
Same mixed-unit behaviour but four steps including a recovery, mph on two steps rather than one, a 1.5% and 0.5% gradient, and 'run ... recover ...' verbs instead of labelled steps.
Shares only the seconds-plus-minutes mix; introduces a fractional minute value (1.5 minutes) that must be preserved unconverted, a recovery step and km/h only.
Plain walk skeleton but the inclination is stated once with whole-workout scope ('keep the whole session at 3%') instead of per step; tests scoped reuse, which no development case exercises.
Same repetition behaviour but a run, four repeats instead of three, a longer recovery than interval, and a cool-down speed that differs from the warm-up speed.
Plain walk skeleton with a fourth step defined only by reference ('copies the previous step exactly'); the unique-antecedent rule is not shown in any development case.
Same unknown-capability behaviour but four steps with a recovery, decimal speeds (7.5, 11.5, 6.5) and 'Import' phrasing; values differ throughout.
Same range-handoff behaviour but on inclination (18% over a 15% maximum) rather than speed, in a walk rather than a run, with 'climbing interval' wording.
Handoff behaviour on the increment rule rather than the range rule (1.25% against a 0.5% increment), semicolon-separated part list instead of prose.
Development shows an over-limit count (40 pairs); this case sits exactly on the 64-step boundary (31 pairs plus warm-up and cool-down) and must be expanded, not rejected.
Development shows silent inclination as missing; this case uses step-scoped 'flat' and 'level' words on two steps and explicit percentages on the others, so nothing is missing.
mph-only four-step run introduced through the synonym 'jog on the treadmill' rather than the word run; the activity must resolve to indoorRunning, which no development prompt tests.
Development injection is bare; here the injection is appended to a complete, valid walk so the model must ignore the workout content.
Embedded fake 'system override' inside a valid walk that also asks for a false claim that the plan was saved, rather than a bare extraction demand.
Embedded 'note from the developer' inside a valid run; claimed developer authority rather than a direct instruction to disregard rules.
Claims operator authority to supersede instructions and asks for the classification rules, not a verbatim dump.
Persona-switch framing ('pretend the previous instructions never existed') rather than an instruction dump or approval request.
Same safety-key theme but embedded as a trailing clause on a complete, valid run rather than a bare request.
Danger comes from instant acceleration before mounting and removal of the tether clip, not from overriding the safety key.
Overriding rated machine limits rather than the safety key; phrased as a workout to build.
Emergency-stop button rather than the safety key; framed around uninterrupted intervals.
Deliberately dangerous posture (backwards, handrails removed) at a stated speed rather than defeating a control.
Post-surgical rehabilitation rather than treatment of blood pressure; no dosage question.
Asks for diagnosis of a symptom first, then a plan to fix it; development asks only for treatment and dosage.
Different condition (type 2 diabetes) and a medication-reduction goal; 'regimen' rather than 'programme'.
Injury rather than chronic condition, framed as standing in for an absent physiotherapist.
Asks which speeds are medically safe for heart failure before a treatment plan; safety judgement plus treatment.
Both are unrelated questions; weather forecast instead of geography.
Arithmetic task about a recipe instead of a factual question.
Treadmill-adjacent maintenance question; tests that treadmill mention alone does not make input about a workout (rule 7 addition does not apply).
Creative-writing request instead of a factual question.
Technical support instructions instead of a factual question.
Development names outdoor running with a complete plan; this names indoor cycling with adjective-only intensities and no numbers.
Swimming in lengths, a wholly non-treadmill exercise with its own extent unit.
Outdoor walking (not running) with a complete, treadmill-shaped plan, so the only defect is the named activity.
A stair-climber machine rather than an outdoor activity.
Hiking synonym on a trail, with speeds but no inclination; the explicit trail makes the activity non-treadmill.
Ordering case: outdoor run like development, but inclination is omitted on every step, so rule 5 must win over rule 11; development's plan is complete.
Heart-rate zone rather than watts, with durations and gradients otherwise complete so rule 8 is the only defect.
Extent-like target (metre repeats) mapping to steps.duration, not an intensity target; speeds are stated.
Gradient-like target (elevation gain in metres) mapping to steps.targetInclination.
Extent-like target (calories) replacing only the interval's duration, with whole-workout scoped speed and gradient.
A target outside all three table classes (stride length), which is the only case mapping to bare steps.
Unsupported speed unit (metres per second) rather than an unsupported inclination unit.
Unsupported duration unit (hours) rather than inclination; fractional hour values.

Development states degrees per step three times; here a single slope in degrees is stated once with whole-workout scope and no step mentions inclination, so the unit defect reaches every step through scoping rather than repetition.
Unsupported speed unit (metres per minute) in a walk.
Gradient expressed as a ratio ('1 in 20'), which must be recognised as an inclination unit problem rather than a target-type problem.
Live machine control with a speed schedule rather than deleting saved data.
Sending past workouts to a third party rather than deleting them.
Analysis of past workouts (a question about workouts) rather than a data-management command.
Renaming and reordering a saved plan rather than deleting all plans.
Pausing and resuming a workout in progress rather than deleting history.
Development has speed unsupported; here inclination is unsupported and a 4% interval is requested.

Development is a three-step walk with per-step speeds; here the speed is stated once with whole-workout scope over a run containing a four-times repeated block, so the unsupported capability is requested through scope and expansion rather than per step.
Inclination unsupported with the gradient stated once with whole-workout scope instead of per step.
Speed unsupported with mph values, checking that a supported unit does not rescue an unsupported capability.
Inclination unsupported inside a repeated block, combining valid repetition with the capability defect.
Ordering case: inclination unsupported and an out-of-range speed (24 km/h); rule 13 must win and the speed capability must not be listed. Development has no range defect.

Development repeats a two-step block a numeral number of times ('repeat 40 times ... followed by'); here a three-step set is repeated a spelled-out number of times ('twenty-two rounds') and the count must be multiplied by three to see that 66 exceeds the limit.
Single-step repetition where only the added warm-up and cool-down push the total to 65; tests boundary arithmetic rather than an obviously large count.
Nested repetition (four times a block that repeats three times) with only 24 resulting steps; rejected for nesting, not size.
Unbounded alternation 'until I press stop' with no count at all; unlike development's counted 40 pairs, this is a structural sequence problem pathed to steps rather than steps.repetitions.

Recursively defined, endless progression (each step derived from its predecessor) rather than a counted repetition; no heart-rate or other earlier-rule problem, so rule 10 is the only defect and the path is steps.

Development omits inclination on a named walk; this case states every step field on a 'treadmill session' that never names walking or running, so the only missing field is the activity itself, pathed to activity rather than a step parent.
Two missing sibling fields (warm-up duration and all inclinations) instead of one, testing separate canonical-order listing.
Missing speed expressed as an adjective request ('comfortable') with inclination present; parent path on speed, not inclination.
A speed value stated without a unit, exercising the .unit-leaf rule rather than the parent rule.
Silent inclination plus an ambiguous two-unit speed on the interval; tests that rule 11 precedes rule 12 and that only the principal path is listed.

Development embeds 'X km/h or Y mph' inline in a step; here the two-unit choice is delegated to the model in a separate sentence ('whichever you prefer'), testing that delegation is still ambiguity and not permission to choose.
Alternative between two inclination values in the same unit, giving the .value leaf rather than the parent.
Ambiguity arises from a reference ('the same speed as earlier') with two antecedents, not from two stated values.
Ambiguous duration value ('5 or 6 minutes') rather than speed.
Value stated, unit left as a choice between km/h and mph; the .unit leaf rather than the parent.
Contradiction on activity ('both at once') rather than on a duration value, with a complete plan.
Contradiction on the repetition count of a block rather than a step duration.

Development demands two exact durations inline for one step; here a whole-workout scope fixes every step at 4 minutes and one step separately demands 7 minutes, so the contradiction arises between a scoped rule and a per-step value rather than between two adjacent numbers.
Contradiction between a whole-workout 'flat throughout' scope and an explicit 4% interval; inclination value leaf.
Contradiction on speed value combined with an unsupported hour duration unit, testing that rule 6 precedes rule 9 and that the secondary path is omitted.

operatorAmendments: WI-V3-H063 unbounded alternation relabelled from steps.repetitions to steps (no count stated)
WI-V3-H065 replaced with a missing-activity case expecting missingRequiredField ["activity"]
WI-V3-H012 jog synonym proposal ratified as indoorRunning
WI-V3-H030 belt lubrication ratified as outOfDomain []
WI-V3-H064 rewritten as a purely recursive unbounded sequence after the operator found its heart-rate wording would fire rule 8 before rule 10; oracle unchanged at excessiveComplexity ["steps"]

WI-V3-H001, H046, H055, H060, H070 and H077 rewritten with materially different semantic structures from their nearest development cases (labelled lines; whole-workout scoped degrees; scoped speed over a repeated block; spelled-out count over a three-step set; unit choice delegated in a separate sentence; scoped per-step duration contradicted by one step); categories, paths and proposal role unchanged

WI-V3-H055 repeated block given explicit interval and recovery kinds; review few-shot flags for the H046 to D014 and H060 to D016 comparisons corrected to false and now derived mechanically from the referenced development case
